title: What are the Pros and Cons of Heat Pumps?
channel: Monkey Wrench Plumbing, Heating, Air & Electric
summary: An HVAC company lists heat pump pros (efficiency over electric heat, two-in-one, no combustion, zoning) and cons (higher cost than an AC, higher electric bills, maintenance, weaker below 25°F).

assertions.quote: about 50 percent less energy consumed when heating a home compared to Standard Electric heating systems
since a heat pump houses both Heating and Cooling elements
running a gas or oil-based furnace introduces several pitfalls for one there is the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning

verdicts.note: An electric heat pump has no combustion, so it removes that carbon monoxide source, though other gas appliances may remain.

assertions.quote: each indoor air handler is controllable to ensure that your family can attain their ideal Comfort

verdicts.note: Each ductless indoor head has its own controls, giving zoned heating and cooling.
Owners reported more control over individual rooms' temperatures as a main non-energy benefit, and some kept central systems precisely because mini-splits let them set points room by room.
Each indoor head of a mini-split warms or cools a single room or zone, and one outdoor unit serves up to four zones.

assertions.quote: heat pumps are on average five percent more expensive than traditional air conditioners
heat pumps may require more maintenance than a standard air conditioner but this is because they have more moving Parts
anything below 40 degrees will cause the heat pump's efficiency to slip and it will need to consume more power
